value.body: A product manager decides what a product will do and why, and works with engineering, design and business teams to build and launch it. Software product companies, startups, fintech and e-commerce firms hire them. A day involves talking to users, writing requirements, prioritising features, reviewing data and running team meetings.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Engineering or business degree; often an MBA or prior work experience

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Jira, analytics dashboards, SQL, Excel, wireframing tools

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Direct fresher product manager roles are few. Common routes are associate product manager (APM) programmes, moving in from analyst, engineering or business roles after a few years, or an MBA followed by campus hiring.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Understanding user problems through research and data
Writing clear requirements and user stories
Communicating across engineering, design and business teams

value.title: At a glance
items: Many product managers spend two to five years in another role first.
Common next roles: senior product manager, group product manager, head of product.
The role carries responsibility for outcomes without direct authority over the team.
